title: Maverick Spend
summary: Spend outside approved vendors, contracts, or purchasing policy.
whyPeCares: PE cares because this KPI gives an early read on growth quality, margin expansion, cash conversion, execution discipline, or exit-story credibility.
goodBadSignals: Good performance shows controlled execution and improving unit economics; bad performance signals leakage, weak process ownership, or a diligence risk requiring deeper segmentation.
improvementActions: Standardize the definition and data owner.
Segment by customer, site, product, team, or channel.
Tie movement to an operating playbook and weekly cadence.

articleSections.title: Strategic Context & Value Driver
body: In the pursuit of procurement-led value creation, Maverick Spend is the 'Silent Killer' of negotiated margins. We define maverick spend as any purchase made outside of authorized contracts, preferred vendor lists, or established procurement protocols. In the early stages of a private equity hold, unmanaged maverick spend can erode up to 30-40% of the savings negotiated during the '100-Day' sourcing workstream, effectively neutralizing the GP's efforts to professionalize the supply chain.

From an Operating Partner's perspective, maverick spend is a symptom of fragmented organizational authority and poor financial controls. It typically occurs when business units or individual managers bypass centralized procurement to maintain legacy relationships or to avoid the perceived 'friction' of formal approval workflows. By eliminating this 'rogue' purchasing behavior, we not only capture immediate P&L savings but also reset the organizational culture toward one of accountability and fiscal discipline, which is essential for scaling the asset.

The strategic driver for controlling maverick spend is the maximization of 'Purchasing Leverage.' When spend is fragmented across hundreds of non-preferred vendors, the portfolio company loses its ability to negotiate volume-based discounts and favorable payment terms. By funneling all addressable spend through a handful of strategic partners, we create the commercial density required to extract 'Procurement Alpha.' Controlling maverick spend is therefore a prerequisite for the more advanced category management strategies that drive long-term margin expansion.
articleSections.callout: Maverick spend is the enemy of scale—you cannot leverage what you cannot control.

articleSections.title: Operational Levers & Benchmarking
body: The primary operational lever for eliminating maverick spend is the implementation of a 'Strict Procurement Policy' backed by automated 'Hard Stops' in the financial system. We benchmark maverick spend rates against a 'Best-in-Class' standard of <5% for all addressable categories. Achieving this requires a rigorous 'Spend Visibility' exercise, where we use AI-driven classification tools to flag any invoice that does not match an approved purchase order or a contracted vendor in the master data file.

Another critical lever is the 'Catalog-Led' buying model, where employees are directed to a pre-approved portal for their daily purchasing needs. This 'Guided Buying' experience reduces the temptation for employees to search for alternative vendors, as the preferred options are made the 'easiest' to buy from. We also implement 'Root-Cause' reporting, where business unit leaders are required to justify any non-compliant spend during monthly operational reviews, creating a 'culture of consequences' that discourages bypass behavior over time.

Benchmarking maverick spend also involves analyzing 'Category-Specific' compliance. We often find that categories like IT hardware, marketing services, and facilities maintenance have the highest rates of non-contracted spend due to their 'specialized' nature. By benchmarking these categories individually against industry peers, the Operating Partner can identify specific 'leakage points' and deploy targeted remediation plans, such as renegotiating the tail-spend or consolidating local service providers into a national agreement. Benchmarking is the diagnostic tool that reveals where the margin is being lost.

articleSections.title: Math & Unit Economics (Example Injection)
body: Consider a $400M industrial services business with $150M in annual indirect spend. The procurement team has negotiated a national contract for MRO (Maintenance, Repair, and Operations) supplies with a 15% discount versus legacy local pricing. However, due to poor policy enforcement, 40% of the MRO spend—roughly $12M—remains 'maverick,' being purchased by local plant managers from local hardware stores at full retail price, effectively ignoring the $1.8M in potential annual savings.

By implementing a 'No PO, No Pay' policy and mandating the use of a centralized MRO catalog, the Operating Partner reduces maverick spend from 40% to 5% within two quarters. This shift brings an additional $10.5M of spend under the national contract, yielding $1.57M in immediate, annualized EBITDA uplift. The 'Cost of Compliance'—including the software license and a procurement coordinator—is approximately $200k, resulting in a nearly 8x return on the investment in maverick spend control.

On an enterprise value basis, this $1.57M in found EBITDA is worth $18.8M at a 12x exit multiple. If the GP allows the 40% maverick rate to persist throughout the five-year hold, they are effectively 'gifting' nearly $20M of EV to the next owner. This math illustrates why Operating Partners prioritize maverick spend as a 'Day 1' initiative; it is one of the fastest and most reliable ways to drive 'Operational Alpha' with minimal capital expenditure or organizational disruption.

articleSections.title: Technology & Tooling Stack
body: To combat maverick spend effectively, we deploy a modern 'Procure-to-Pay' (P2P) platform such as Coupa, Basware, or SAP Ariba. these platforms act as the 'Digital Front Door' for all spending, offering an Amazon-like shopping experience that directs users toward contracted items and preferred vendors. The P2P system's automated approval workflows ensure that every dollar of spend is reviewed by the appropriate budget owner before the commitment is made, virtually eliminating 'after-the-fact' invoice approvals.

We also utilize 'Spend Analytics' software like SpendHQ or GEP Strategy to perform 'Post-Transaction' audits. These tools ingest data directly from the ERP (e.g., NetSuite, Sage Intacct) and use fuzzy-matching logic to identify vendors that provide similar services to our preferred partners but are not on the approved list. This 'Spend Leakage' dashboard allows the procurement team to identify 'Persistent Mavericks' and intervene before the non-compliant behavior becomes institutionalized.

Finally, we integrate these tools with 'Virtual Card' solutions like Brex, Ramp, or Airbase for discretionary T&E and small-dollar purchases. These platforms allow the Operating Partner to set granular 'Spend Limits' and 'Category Restrictions' at the individual card level, ensuring that even 'Tail Spend' is captured and managed within the broader compliance framework. This combination of front-end guided buying and back-end analytics creates a 'Closed-Loop' spend management environment that maximizes margin capture and provides a clean audit trail for future buyers.

articleSections.title: Exit Readiness & Multiple Expansion
body: As we prepare for exit, a low maverick spend rate is a powerful proxy for 'Management Maturity' and 'Operational Control.' A buyer will conduct deep procurement diligence, looking for evidence that the company's EBITDA is supported by a disciplined and predictable cost structure. By demonstrating that >95% of spend is under contracted control, we provide the buyer with the confidence that the margin profile is sustainable and that there are no 'hidden' costs or legacy liabilities waiting to emerge after the transaction.

The 'Procurement Audit Trail' generated by the P2P and analytics stack becomes a core part of the exit narrative. We present the 'Compliance Bridge'—showing how maverick spend was systematically reduced and how that discipline has protected the company's gross margins through various market cycles. This visibility allows the seller to negotiate for a 'Professionalization Premium,' as the business is seen as a 'Plug-and-Play' asset that is ready for further scaling under a new owner without significant integration risk.

Ultimately, controlling maverick spend contributes to multiple expansion by de-risking the 'Expense-Side' of the P&L. A business with tight spend controls is seen as having higher 'Earnings Quality' than a peer where spending is discretionary and unmanaged. By institutionalizing maverick spend control as a core business process, we ensure that the value created during the hold period is fully realized at exit, maximizing the IRR for the fund and cementing the Operating Partner's reputation as a disciplined value creator.
